1. Tuatha defender office: sovereign protector, gate-holder, law shield; Tuatha Dé Danann: divine tribes, craft, sovereignty, otherworld descent

Humans later copied fragments of this being into myth, ritual, monster lore, and sacred art, but the Deity is the older source: Tuatha defender office: sovereign protector, gate-holder, law shield; Tuatha Dé Danann: divine tribes, craft, sovereignty, otherworld descent. Ancient humans saw this being through the Mythos Gate and copied what they saw as myth, but the Deity is the SOURCE, not the copy.

2. REALM ANATOMY
   - Avalora fae-root anatomy with silver-branch nerves, moonlit skin, thorn-bloom scars, mist-vein translucence, geas marks, and living bark/flesh borders These are NOT biological features — they are DIVINE PHYSIOLOGY grown from the realm itself. The skin is not skin but living divine material. The veins are not veins but energy channels.

3. VISUAL IDENTITY

The design must feel older than human mythology and avoid generic elf, wood block giant, treehouse body, cute fairy wings, random Celtic clipart knots, Renaissance costume. - Bare head — NO halo rings, NO discs, NO circles behind or around the head. The head is completely bare.
- Every element of the body must feel like it GREW from divine anatomy, not like it was PUT ON as costume.

WEAPON: Dagoran Bulwark Lugh Silver-Spear Thornblade
The weapon is made of the same divine material as the body — it looks like an EXTENSION of the deity, not a separate object. It is held with deliberate purpose, not generic combat posing. The weapon's silhouette must be unique to this deity and not shared by any other.
